newsitem.title: USA: BASF to cut 128 jobs, close facility in Bedford, Mass..
newsitem.headline: BASF to cut 128 jobs, close facility in Bedford, Mass..

text.p: BASF Corp. said Wednesday that it was exiting the magnetic tape business in North America, which will result in the elimination of 128 jobs and the closure of its facility in Bedford, Mass.

BASF, a unit of Germany's BASF AG, said that at the end of the year it will discontinue handling the magnetic tape business in the United States and Canada for BASF Magnetics GmbH of Germany, which will begin using independent distributors for its products. The retail audio/video cassettes business will be discontinued, it added.

"We have reached a determination that this business, not being a core business, is no longer viable for BASF Corporation," Eggert Voscherau, president of BASF's Consumer Products and Life Science Division, said in a statement.

The company, based in Mount Olive, N.J., said its BASF Magnetics Corp. facility in Bedford will be closed and about 115 employees, mainly involved in sales and marketing, will be offered severance packages. In addition, about 13 employees in similar functions in Toronto, Canada, will be let go.

BASF provides a wide range of products, including chemicals, plastics, fibers, automotive and industrial coatings, dispersions and paper chemicals, dyes and pigments, agricultural products, pharmaceuticals and vitamins. It employs about 14,000 people.
